United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

title.narrative: Strengthening open science and Science, Technology, and Innovation ecosystems in Chile and Ecuador, enhancing access for all, including the most vulnerable populations, particularly in terms of gender equality in science, evidence-based policymaking, and science literacy

description.narrative:
In both Chile and Ecuador, there is growing interest in strengthening public engagement with science and fostering collaboration among researchers, educators, communities, and decision-makers.
Foster open science policies/initiatives provide opportunities for individuals and communities to participate directly in knowledge generation and iteration. The UNESCO Recommendation on Open Science provides an internationally agreed definition, as well as a set of shared values and guiding principles for open science and identifies a set of actions conducive to a fair and equitable operationalization of open science for all, being a relevant means to achieve stronger engagement and setting national practices without risking intellectual rights, encouraging scientists to develop tools and methods for managing data so that as much data as possible can be shared, as appropriate.
During the 2026–2027 biennium, UNESCO will support actions that strengthen open science and SYI ecosystems in both countries, fostering exchanges and collaboration when appropriate. UNESCO will foster partnerships with research institutions promoting. e.g., marine science, water sciences, biodiversity, geology and fundamental sciences., identifying trends and opportunities to mainstream the UNESCO open science recommendation.
Dissemination activities and endorsing gender transformative initiatives that foster women in sciences will be also conducted, leveraging on the materials already developed by UNESCO, tailoring them on a case by case scenario.
